thread:
maya: heads up — we're getting a new p95/p99 hump starting ~06:50 UTC after the traffic ramp. multiple customers reporting ~2-4s extra latency. tagging support.
ingress-bot: ALERT: ingress.p95 increased by 2.3s (5m window) — service: api-ingress, region: eu-west-1, affected_routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat
lisa: seeing customer tickets from acme and glide.ai, both saying responses stall then come back. attaching customer ids in the ticket.
ben: quick hypothesis: worker pool warmup + admission control causing queueing. after ramp the pools didn't spin up fast enough so admission started queuing and we see long tail.
sergio: can you paste the metrics for inflight, queued, and concurrency by pool? particularly embed-serving and gen-serving pools.
maya: posted grafana links: https://grafana/r/abcd  — p95 spike lines up with a rise in queued_requests on gen-serving-eu.
lisa: repro steps from support side: hit /v1/generate with 150 concurrent small prompts over 60s and watch. customers' traffic pattern is a shallow but steady ramp.
ben: grabbing logs — excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T06:51:12Z worker_pool.go:worker=gen-serving-eu active=64 max=64 queued=127 warmup=false
2026-03-17T06:51:13Z admit_control.go:pool=gen-serving-eu admit_act=64 queued=130 drop=0
2026-03-17T06:51:14Z kernel_sched.go:warning kv_miss=0.43 scheduling_delay=120ms
```
sergio: that queued=127/130 with active=64 looks like saturation w/ admission throttle fully engaged. warmup=false suggests the new workers hadn't finished model init but still counted toward max, or warmup stalled.
ben: two immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk): 1) temporarily increase admit limit for gen-serving-eu (64->96) to drain queue; 2) enable fallback routing for non-critical tenants to a smaller model variant (gen-small) to reduce token cost and per-request time.
lisa: can we also add a short-term reduce-cold-start window so more workers stay warm during ramps? that'll help on repeated warmup spikes.
maya: assigning ben to do hotpatch, sergio to monitor metrics + logs, lisa to keep customers updated. ETA for hotpatch?
ben: doing hotpatch now — bumping admit limit for pool gen-serving-eu to 96 and enabling fast-fallback for glide.ai and acme.
ingress-bot: ACTION: admit_limit modified for gen-serving-eu by ben at 06:54 UTC (64 -> 96)
ingress-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: ingress.p95 returned to baseline after admit change; current p95 delta 0.2s (monitored 06:59 — 07:05 UTC)
sergio: post-change metrics look better — queued dropped from 130 -> 10 over ~30s, active climbed to 88 and stabilized. CPU on those hosts spiked but within headroom.
lisa: I've updated the customer tickets: told them we applied a mitigation and will follow up if they still see issues. asked for any recent client SDK rollouts.
maya: next steps: 1) dig into why warmup didn't prefetch kernels (maybe a race in model init), 2) add a short-term runbook step to consider admit limit bump during ramps, 3) consider pre-warm policy for scheduled traffic increases. I'll create an incident follow-up and mark sev-low for now.
ben: opening PR to add a metric-based autoscale warmup (pre-init X workers when queue > threshold) and an emergency admit-bump playbook.
sergio: adding logs and a minis postmortem draft to the shared drive. if anyone sees recurring spikes after the next ramp ping here.
lisa: thanks all :thumbsup:
